general: The five Istari came from the West clothed in the guise of old men, each one carrying a purpose as old as the world and a staff that was more than wood.
Magic in Middle-earth is not spectacle; it is knowledge applied at the right moment, and the greatest of wizards use it least.
The staff of Gandalf was a conduit for a will forged over ages; when it was raised, the obedient world remembered its first instructions.
A spell is simply a word spoken with perfect understanding of what that word means in the oldest of all languages.
The wizards were not sent to wield power against Sauron, but to inspire the free peoples to wield their own — a subtler and more difficult task.
Saruman's voice was the first magic of Orthanc; it could turn the mind of a strong man in the space of a sentence.
There is a fire in Gandalf's eyes that belongs to no wizard born in Middle-earth; it is the flame of something that was present at the beginning.
The palantíri were not magic but technology of a forgotten age; the wizardry was in knowing which truths to trust and which to doubt.
Magic leaves traces in the world, grooves worn by repeated use, and the oldest spells are carved deep into the fabric of reality.
Radagast the Brown knew the language of birds and the medicine of roots, and in his own way kept more darkness at bay than anyone credited him for.
An Istar does not age as men age; they diminish or they fall, and the manner of the falling reveals what was always at the core of them.
gandalf: I am Olórin who walked unseen among the elves and learned their sorrows, and I am Mithrandir to those who need a grey wanderer.
My staff is not my power — it is my invitation to the world to cooperate, and the world, being old and set in its ways, usually obliges.
I have returned from death clothed in white, and I find I am no less irritable for the experience — if anything, somewhat more.
The fireworks are a courtesy; what I truly bring to the Shire is a question, and a question at the right moment changes everything.
Saruman believes it is only great power that can hold evil in check, but that is not what I have found; I have found that it is small things.
I was Gandalf the Grey; now I am Gandalf the White, and the difference is something I understand better in practice than in theory.
A wizard's business is his own; but if you insist on knowing, I have been kindling fires in cold hearts across the length of Middle-earth.
When Bilbo said he felt like butter scraped over too much bread, I recognized the metaphor — the Ring was already beginning its work.
The secret of Glamdring is that it is very sharp; the secret of wisdom is the same.
frodo: I used to think Gandalf was primarily a producer of excellent fireworks; I have since revised that assessment considerably.
He gave me a task I did not want and could not refuse, and I think he knew exactly what he was doing, which I find both reassuring and infuriating.
sam: Gandalf always knows more than he lets on, which is either very comforting or very unsettling depending on what you're hoping he knows about your situation.
A wizard is never late, Mr. Frodo; that's what he says. I've noticed he never says he's never early on purpose either.
